items.t: Snap settles lawsuit accusing platform of fueling teen depression and eating disorders
items.d: The plaintiffs said they started using YouTube as young as age 3 and other social media platforms at around age 9 and developed compulsive usage habits that they attributed to features such as autoplay and infinite scrolling.
items.fullText: In Brief Posted: 11:11 AM PST · November 2, 2026 Image Credits: KIRILL KUDRYAVTSEV/AFP / Getty Images Aisha Malik Snap settles lawsuit accusing platform of fueling teen depression and eating disorders Snap has reached a settlement in a lawsuit brought by two teenagers who accused the company of designing its platform to be addictive and contributing to their depression, anxiety, and eating disorders, as first reported by Reuters . The plaintiffs had previously reached settlements with Meta, TikTok, and YouTube. The trial was set to be Snap’s first in a broader wave of litigation over social media’s impact on young users. The company had already settled its other cases scheduled for trial. Snap CEO Evan Spiegel was expected to take the stand. The plaintiffs said they started using YouTube as young as age 3 and other social media platforms at around age 9. They said they developed compulsive usage habits, which they attributed to features such as autoplay and infinite scrolling. “The Parties are pleased to have been able to resolve this matter in an amicable manner,” a Snap spokesperson said in a statement to TechCrunch. “We’ve built safeguards, launched safety tutorials, and partnered with experts and because safety is never finished, we remain committed to continually strengthening the safety, privacy, and well-being of our community.” Social media giants are facing thousands of lawsuits in federal and state courts over claims that they knowingly designed their platforms to hook young users and fuel a youth mental health crisis involving anxiety, depression, and suicide. items.fullText: Slice Into GFN Thursday: ‘Phantom Blade Zero’ Launches on GeForce NOW S-GAME’s kungfupunk action arrives at launch alongside nine games this week — plus, a ‘World of Warcraft: Forever’ reward is coming soon. October 29, 2026 by GeForce NOW Community 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! This Halloween week, GFN Thursday is delivering a fresh batch of gaming treats. Something wicked this blade comes. S-GAME’s Phantom Blade Zero launches on GeForce NOW today, bringing a scarily good blend of martial arts and punk fantasy to the cloud. There’s also something on the horizon for adventurers: World of Warcraft: Forever arrives Wednesday, Nov. 4 at 3 p.m. PST, with a launch-week access reward coming for GeForce NOW members. This week’s lineup also includes nine games streaming from the GeForce NOW library , alongside new mod support for Cyberpunk 2077 and The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered . That means more options to play, with no downloads or installs to haunt gamers’ devices . There’s another sweet update for gamers in India: The option to sign up for four-month Performance and Ultimate memberships is launching tomorrow. Visit the GeForce NOW website for more information. Cold Steel Meets Cloud Power Framed for his master’s murder and gravely wounded, a warrior named Soul has 66 days to uncover a conspiracy threatening the martial world in S-GAME’s Phantom Blade Zero . Powered by Unreal Engine 5, the game combines wuxia storytelling with cinematic action. Master more than 30 primary weapons and over 20 Phantom Edges, chaining evasions, deflections and counterattacks into fluid combat. Traditional Chinese martial arts meet mechanical prosthetics, industrial ruins and rock music in a distinctive kungfupunk world. Ultimate members can wield GeForce RTX 5080-class performance in the cloud across PCs, Macs, handhelds, mobile devices, browsers, compatible TVs and more. It’s all part of six games joining the GeForce NOW library this week. Deployment Without the Downloads Squad up and answer the call on the cloud. items.fullText: Google Cloud and NVIDIA Announce General Availability of NVIDIA Vera Rubin Infrastructure Google Cloud A5X instances, accelerated by NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, support European innovators with next-generation agentic and reinforcement learning infrastructure. October 21, 2026 by Uttara Kumar 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! General availability of the instances is coming next month, with planned expansion of availability to Europe — bringing an integrated platform for training, inference and large-scale reinforcement learning to cloud customers. A5X instances bring together NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72, NVIDIA ConnectX-9 SuperNICs, Google Cloud Virgo Network and Google Cloud’s fourth-generation advanced liquid-cooling technology for demanding agentic inference and reinforcement learning workloads at scale. Google Cloud plans to scale its Vera Rubin-based infrastructure to as many as 960,000 Rubin GPUs across multiple sites. Ineffable Intelligence , a London-based technology company founded by AlphaGo creator David Silver, was the first customer to access A5X. Ineffable is using the platform to advance large-scale reinforcement learning and shape “superlearner” systems that learn continuously from experience. items.fullText: NVIDIA Cloud Partners Scale Across Europe — Sovereign, Open and Built for Safe AI Agents Growing ecosystem of AI clouds across Europe, Nordics, Africa and Central Asia build full-stack NVIDIA DSX Vera Rubin AI factories as AI-native companies drive demand for sovereign compute, training, inference and post-training services. October 21, 2026 by Stuart Pitts 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Demand from AI-natives is pulling the European AI cloud ecosystem forward faster than ever. Developers need compute closer to their data, open models they can customize and serve at scale, and full-stack infrastructure that is secure by design. NVIDIA Cloud Partners across Europe, the Nordics, Africa, and Central Asia are expanding regional compute capacity for model training and inference, helping developers build agentic and physical AI applications, and establishing boundaries around what agents can access and do. Together, they’re turning Europe’s energy, data, research and industrial expertise into productive intelligence — supporting new models, applications, organizations and jobs while giving people more control over where and how they develop and deploy AI. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Sovereign: AI Clouds Building European AI Infrastructure Europe is home to world-class research, engineering talent, industrial expertise, data, the next generation of models and applications that requires large-scale computing close to where that knowledge resides. Regional AI clouds provide the infrastructure foundation on which model builders, enterprises and entire industries can grow. As AI factories scale, power becomes a constraint which makes it critical for every watt to produce more intelligence. Nscale is using the NVIDIA DSX Platform to coordinate power allocation with workload requirements.
